itemdesc-philosophersstone: Right-click a block to transmute it into its neighbour in a chain (stone types, wood types, sand ↔ gravel, ...); sneak + right-click goes the other way. Tool-mode key: 1x1, 3x3 or 5x5 at once. Right-click in the air to open the crafting grid. Free, and never used up when crafting with it.
itemdesc-transmutationtablet: A transmutation table you carry: right-click to open it anywhere.
itemdesc-arcanetablet: A Transmutation Tablet with a crafting grid. Right-click to open the tablet; sneak + right-click (or the button in the tablet) to open its crafting window. In the handbook, Emc Craft under a crafting recipe fills the grid from your EMC, and ingredients you haven't learned are marked red. Tools you carry are used; missing ones are made from EMC and burned back into EMC when you close the window.
emccraft-hint: Craft as in your inventory's grid. Emc Craft in the handbook fills this grid from your EMC. Closing the window gives back what's left in it (to your inventory, or at your feet if it's full) and burns tools made from EMC back into EMC.
error-emccraft-notablet: You need an Arcane Tablet with you for that.
error-emccraft-norecipe: That recipe ({0}) wasn't found on the server.
error-emccraft-missing: You haven't learned anything that can be used for: {0}.
error-emccraft-notmakeable: These can't be made from EMC (no value, or the server keeps them out of transmutation): {0}.
itemdesc-alchemicalfuel-alchemicalcoal: Burns at 1,400 °C for 160 seconds. In a forge it lasts 4x as long and burns 200 °C hotter.
itemdesc-alchemicalfuel-mobiusfuel: Burns at 1,500 °C for 640 seconds; 4x as long in a forge.
itemdesc-alchemicalfuel-aeternalisfuel: Burns at 1,600 °C for 2,560 seconds; the base of dark matter.
itemdesc-matter-dark: Condensed EMC: 8 aeternalis fuel around a temporal gear. Makes tier 5 tools and armour that never wear out; 4 make a dark matter block.
itemdesc-matter-red: Denser still: 3 dark matter between 6 aeternalis fuel. Makes tier 6 tools and armour that never wear out; 4 make a red matter block.
itemdesc-mattertool-dark-pickaxe: Digs stone, ore and metal at speed 9; 3x3 at once with the tool-mode key (sneak for one block). 3.5 attack. Tier 5; never wears out.
itemdesc-mattertool-dark-shovel: Digs soil, sand, gravel and snow at speed 9; 3x3 at once with the tool-mode key (sneak for one block). 3.5 attack. Tier 5; never wears out.
itemdesc-mattertool-dark-axe: Chops wood at speed 9 and fells whole trees; 3x3 at once with the tool-mode key. 5 attack. Tier 5; never wears out.
itemdesc-mattertool-dark-sword: 8 attack (a steel falx does 5.25), reach 2.75 blocks. Tier 5; never wears out. Right-click: strikes every hostile creature within 6 blocks for 8 EMC each; sneak + right-click in the air: every creature but players and pets.
itemdesc-mattertool-dark-hoe: Tills soil into farmland; digs soil and plants at speed 5. Tier 5; never wears out.
itemdesc-mattertool-dark-hammer: Smashes stone, ore and other hard blocks at speed 8, 3x3 at a time (sneak or the tool-mode key for one block). 5 attack. Tier 5; never wears out.
itemdesc-mattertool-red-pickaxe: Digs stone, ore and metal at speed 14; 3x3 or 5x5 at once with the tool-mode key (sneak for one block). 4.5 attack. Tier 6; never wears out. Also 3 tall, 3 wide or 3 long with the tool-mode key.
itemdesc-mattertool-red-shovel: Digs soil, sand, gravel and snow at speed 14; 3x3 or 5x5 at once with the tool-mode key (sneak for one block). 4.5 attack. Tier 6; never wears out. Also 3 tall, 3 wide or 3 long with the tool-mode key.
itemdesc-mattertool-red-axe: Chops wood at speed 14 and fells whole trees; 3x3 or 5x5 at once with the tool-mode key. 7 attack. Tier 6; never wears out. Also 3 tall, 3 wide or 3 long with the tool-mode key.
itemdesc-mattertool-red-sword: 11 attack (a steel falx does 5.25), reach 2.75 blocks. Tier 6; never wears out. Right-click: strikes every hostile creature within 6 blocks for 8 EMC each; sneak + right-click in the air: every creature but players and pets. Tool-mode key: 3x3, 5x5, 3 tall, 3 wide or 3 long.
itemdesc-mattertool-red-hoe: Tills soil into farmland; digs soil and plants at speed 8. Tier 6; never wears out.
itemdesc-mattertool-red-hammer: Smashes stone, ore and other hard blocks at speed 12, 3x3 or 5x5 at a time (sneak or the tool-mode key for one block). 7 attack. Tier 6; never wears out. Also 3 tall, 3 wide or 3 long with the tool-mode key.
blockdesc-transmutationtable: Right-click to open. Burn items into EMC to learn them (or drop them on Learn to keep them), then create anything you know from your EMC. Closes if you walk more than 10 blocks away; a hopper or chute pointing into it feeds it items to burn, 16 a second, while its owner is online.
blockdesc-energycollector-mk1: Makes up to 4 EMC a second in full sunlight (less in shade, none in the dark), stores 10,000, and feeds condensers, furnaces and relays next to it every second. Sneak + right-click with an empty hand or a Klein star to take the EMC. Right-click with a Klein star to put it in: it is charged at the collector's rate before anything else; right-click with an empty hand to take it out.
blockdesc-energycollector-mk2: Makes up to 12 EMC a second in full sunlight (less in shade, none in the dark), stores 30,000, and feeds condensers, furnaces and relays next to it every second. Sneak + right-click with an empty hand or a Klein star to take the EMC. Right-click with a Klein star to put it in: it is charged at the collector's rate before anything else; right-click with an empty hand to take it out.
blockdesc-energycollector-mk3: Makes up to 40 EMC a second in full sunlight (less in shade, none in the dark), stores 60,000, and feeds condensers, furnaces and relays next to it every second. Sneak + right-click with an empty hand or a Klein star to take the EMC. Right-click with a Klein star to put it in: it is charged at the collector's rate before anything else; right-click with an empty hand to take it out.
blockdesc-energycondenser-mk1: Put an item in the target slot: burns up to 20 other items a second (plus EMC from collectors) into up to 20 copies of the target a second, as in ProjectE. Stores 10,000,000 EMC; 40 storage slots. A Klein star in the target slot is charged instead of copied.
blockdesc-energycondenser-mk2: Put an item in the target slot: burns up to 64 other items a second (plus EMC from collectors) into up to 64 copies of the target a second. Stores 10,000,000 EMC; 40 storage slots. A Klein star in the target slot is charged instead of copied.
gui-burn-hint: Drop an item on Burn to turn it into EMC and learn it (left-click: the whole stack, right-click: one). Drop it on Learn to learn it and keep it. Drop a Klein star on Charge to fill it from your EMC (right-click: empty it into your EMC); on Burn it's burned for the star and what it holds.
error-charge-notstar: Only Klein stars go in Charge; {0} isn't one.
gui-create-hint: Left-click: take one  ·  Right-click: take a stack  ·  Shift-click: a stack straight into your inventory  ·  Ctrl + right-click: forget (asks first)
heldhelp-stone-craft: Open the crafting grid (right-click in the air)
error-star-full: {0} is full, or you have no EMC to put in it.
condenser-notarget: EMC {0}. Put an item in the target slot.
error-noaccess: You need to be at a transmutation table or carry a transmutation tablet.
error-hascontents: Empty {0} first - it still has things inside.
error-cursorbusy: Put down what you're holding first.
error-notransmutable: The philosopher's stone can't transmute this block.

cmd-recalc: Mapped {0} EMC values in {1} ms from {2} conversions.
cmd-missing: {0} of {1} blocks/items have no EMC value. Biggest groups: {2}. Full list: {3}
cmd-missing-none: All {0} blocks/items in the creative inventory have an EMC value.

chat-announce-cached: Vintage-E version {0}: {1} EMC values (calculated earlier, nothing has changed), {2} missing, {4} value loops (/emc loop).

missing-empty: Nothing is missing - every block and item has an EMC value.
error-noprivilege: Only admins (controlserver privilege) can change EMC values.
missing-select: Click names to select them; Shift-click selects everything in between.
missing-badvalue: Type a number (0 or more) first.
cmdhelp-notadmin: Commands marked (admin) need the controlserver privilege.
cmdhelp-emc: Your EMC, and the EMC value of the item you're holding.
cmdhelp-missing: Opens a searchable list of blocks/items with no EMC value, where you can give them one. Also writes ModData/vintagee/emc-missing.csv.
cmdhelp-set: Gives the held item a fixed EMC value (0 removes its value). Saved to ModConfig/vintagee.json; values are recalculated.
cmdhelp-clear: Removes the fixed value you set for the held item.
cmdhelp-recalc: Recalculates every EMC value from the loaded recipes.
cmdhelp-dump: Writes every value, and what it was worked out from, to ModData/vintagee/emc-values.csv (the chat says where).
cmdhelp-give: Adds EMC to your personal EMC.
cmdhelp-learn: Learns the held item without burning it (anything the transmutation table could burn; admins: anything)
itemdesc-covalencedust-low: Used to build alchemical gear. 40 from 8 stones + 1 charcoal.
itemdesc-covalencedust-medium: Used to build alchemical gear. 40 from 1 iron ingot + 1 saltpeter.
itemdesc-covalencedust-high: Used to build alchemical gear. 40 from 1 diamond + 1 coke.
itemdesc-kleinstar-ein: Holds up to 50,000 EMC; rings, amulets and gadgets draw from it once your own EMC runs out. Right-click: empty it into your EMC; sneak + right-click: fill it. 4 craft into the next size. Can be worn in your emblem slot.
itemdesc-ironband: The base of every ring. 8 iron ingots around 1 alchemical coal.
itemdesc-trinket-blackholeband: While on: pulls loose items within 7 blocks to you, free. Right-click a water or lava source to remove it. On a pedestal: pulls items within 10 blocks into containers next to it. Right-click to switch on or off; can be worn in your hand slot.
itemdesc-trinket-swiftwolfsrendinggale: While on: fly (jump to rise, sneak to sink) and/or a shield that pushes creatures and arrows away within 8 blocks; the tool-mode key picks which and your speed (1x-3x). Flight 6.4 EMC/s x speed, shield 6.4/s. No fall damage while on or 15 s after. Fire key: lightning where you look (64 blocks), 832 EMC, once a second.
itemdesc-trinket-harvestgoddessband: While on: crops within 5 blocks grow (4 EMC per growth stage) and ripe ones are harvested; off, nearby crops still grow slowly for free. Right-click farmland to plant your seeds on empty farmland within 8 blocks. On a pedestal: 8 blocks. Can be worn in your hand slot. Sneak + right-click: harvests every ripe crop within 8 blocks and grows the rest a stage, 4 EMC a stage.
itemdesc-trinket-ignitionring: Carry it and fire can't hurt you. While on: hostile creatures within 5 blocks catch fire and take 3 damage once a second, 4 EMC each. Fire-projectile key: a free fireball (3 damage, sets the target alight, lights torches and burnable blocks). On a pedestal: 8 blocks. Can be worn in your hand slot.
itemdesc-trinket-zeroring: While on: still water within 3 blocks of you freezes into ice, free. On a pedestal: freezes water within 6 blocks and puts out burning creatures. Can be worn in your hand slot. Also lays snow around you. Sneak + right-click: a burst that freezes water and lays snow within 8 blocks, 32 EMC.
itemdesc-trinket-ringofarcana: The Zero Ring (3 blocks), Ignition Ring (5 blocks, 3 damage a second), Harvest Goddess Band (5 blocks) and Swiftwolf's Rending Gale (flight, 8-block shield) in one, all free; the tool-mode key switches each on or off. Fire can't hurt you while you carry it. Can be worn in your hand slot. Sneak + right-click: its freeze and harvest bursts, free. Fire-projectile key: a fireball with Ignition on, else lightning, free.
itemdesc-trinket-bodystone: While on: once you are 100 saturation below full, feeds you up to 200 saturation every 2 seconds for 0.5 EMC each. Tool-mode key: also fill nutrition (1 EMC each, emptiest food group first). On a pedestal: feeds players within 6 blocks 25 saturation a second, free.
itemdesc-trinket-soulstone: While on: heals you 1 health a second for 64 EMC each. On a pedestal: heals players within 6 blocks 0.5 health a second, free.
itemdesc-trinket-lifestone: Body Stone and Soul Stone in one: while on, feeds you (0.5 EMC per saturation) and heals you (64 EMC per health). Tool-mode key: also fill nutrition (1 EMC per saturation). On a pedestal: feeds and heals players within 6 blocks, free.
itemdesc-trinket-mindstone: While on: keeps your body temperature at normal, whatever you wear and whatever the weather, for 1 EMC a second while it has to. Right-click to switch on/off.
itemdesc-trinket-repairtalisman: Always works while you carry it: repairs 1 durability a second on every damaged tool, weapon and piece of armour you carry or wear, and restores clothing 1% a minute. Free. On a pedestal: the same for players within 6 blocks.
itemdesc-trinket-gemofeternaldensity: While on: every 2 seconds it eats junk you carry worth 8 EMC or less (stone, soil, sand, gravel, sticks...) and turns it into its target: iron ingot, gold ingot, diamond, dark matter or red matter (tool-mode key). Leftover EMC is kept for next time. Filter... in its tool modes lists what it may or may not eat. Inside an Alchemical Chest it condenses the chest's contents.
itemdesc-trinket-evertideamulet: Right-click a block to place a water source next to it, free. Fire-projectile key: a ball of water that leaves a source where it lands. On a pedestal: it rains until you take it off.
itemdesc-trinket-volcaniteamulet: Right-click a block to place a lava source next to it, 32 EMC each. Fire-projectile key: a ball of lava (32 EMC) that leaves a source where it lands. Carry it and fire can't hurt you. On a pedestal: clear skies until you take it off.
itemdesc-trinket-watchofflowingtime: While on: time runs 10x faster for the whole world (crops, cooking, curing, day and night) for 8 EMC a second, and crops within 6 blocks grow extra. Tool-mode key: a third as fast instead, for 4 EMC a second, which also slows hostile creatures within 10 blocks. It glows and shows an icon while on (.vintagee to change).
itemdesc-gadget-destructioncatalyst: Right-click a block to break a 3x3 tunnel into it, 1, 4, 8 or 16 blocks deep (tool-mode key), for 8 EMC per block broken. Everything drops where you clicked.
itemdesc-gadget-hyperkineticlens: Right-click or the fire-projectile key shoots an explosive charge that flies straight at 36 blocks a second. Tool-mode key: radius 4, 6, 8 or 10 for 384, 768, 1,536 or 2,304 EMC.
itemdesc-gadget-catalyticlens: Right-click a block to break a 3x3 tunnel 1, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56 or 64 blocks deep (tool-mode key), 8 EMC per block. Fire-projectile key: a radius-10 explosive charge for 2,304 EMC.
itemdesc-gadget-mercurialeye: Sneak + right-click a block to remember it, then right-click blocks to turn them into it: 1x1, 3x3, 5x5, 7x7 or 9x9 of the same block as the one clicked (tool-mode key). You pay the EMC difference, or get it back when the old block was worth more.
itemdesc-gadget-archangelssmite: Right-click: a homing arrow that steers towards hostile creatures (3 damage). Left-click: a volley of 10. Each arrow costs an arrow's EMC.
itemdesc-gadget-tomeofknowledge: Creative mode only: learn everything that can be transmuted.
itemdesc-gadget-diviningrodlow: Right-click a block: the total and average EMC of the 3x3 column below it, 16 blocks deep, and the most valuable block found. Lasts 10x its EMC value in uses.
itemdesc-gadget-diviningrodmedium: Right-click a block: the total and average EMC of the 3x3 column below it, 32 blocks deep, and the most valuable block found. Lasts 10x its EMC value in uses.
itemdesc-gadget-diviningrodhigh: Right-click a block: the total and average EMC of the 3x3 column below it, 128 blocks deep, and the most valuable block found. Lasts 10x its EMC value in uses.
itemdesc-redmattertool-katar: Sword, axe and shears in one: 14 attack, reach 3 blocks; chops wood at speed 16 and fells whole trees; cuts plants and leaves at 14, 3x3 or 5x5 with the tool-mode key. Tier 6; never wears out. Right-click: strikes every hostile creature within 6 blocks for 8 EMC each; sneak + right-click in the air: every creature but players and pets.
itemdesc-redmattertool-morningstar: Pickaxe, shovel and sledgehammer in one: digs stone, ore, metal, soil, sand and gravel at speed 14, 3x3 at a time (5x5 or one block with the tool-mode key). 10 attack. Tier 6; never wears out. Also 3 tall, 3 wide or 3 long with the tool-mode key.
itemdesc-mattertool-dark-shears: Cuts leaves at speed 12 and plants and cloth at 8. Tier 5; never wears out.
itemdesc-mattertool-red-shears: Cuts leaves at speed 18 and plants and cloth at 12. Tier 6; never wears out.
itemdesc-kleinstar-zwei: Holds up to 200,000 EMC; rings, amulets and gadgets draw from it once your own EMC runs out. Right-click: empty it into your EMC; sneak + right-click: fill it. 4 craft into the next size. Can be worn in your emblem slot.
itemdesc-kleinstar-drei: Holds up to 800,000 EMC; rings, amulets and gadgets draw from it once your own EMC runs out. Right-click: empty it into your EMC; sneak + right-click: fill it. 4 craft into the next size. Can be worn in your emblem slot.
itemdesc-kleinstar-vier: Holds up to 3,200,000 EMC; rings, amulets and gadgets draw from it once your own EMC runs out. Right-click: empty it into your EMC; sneak + right-click: fill it. 4 craft into the next size. Can be worn in your emblem slot.
itemdesc-kleinstar-sphere: Holds up to 12,800,000 EMC; rings, amulets and gadgets draw from it once your own EMC runs out. Right-click: empty it into your EMC; sneak + right-click: fill it. 4 craft into the next size. Can be worn in your emblem slot.
itemdesc-kleinstar-omega: Holds up to 51,200,000 EMC; rings, amulets and gadgets draw from it once your own EMC runs out. Right-click: empty it into your EMC; sneak + right-click: fill it. Can be worn in your emblem slot.
itemdesc-alchemicalbag-white: A 32-slot bag. Wear it in a backpack slot. Upgrade it with 4 dark matter for 48 slots.
itemdesc-alchemicalbag-plain: A 32-slot bag. Wear it in a backpack slot. Upgrade it with 4 dark matter for 48 slots.
itemdesc-alchemicalbag-gray: A 32-slot bag. Wear it in a backpack slot. Upgrade it with 4 dark matter for 48 slots.
itemdesc-alchemicalbag-black: A 32-slot bag. Wear it in a backpack slot. Upgrade it with 4 dark matter for 48 slots.
itemdesc-alchemicalbag-brown: A 32-slot bag. Wear it in a backpack slot. Upgrade it with 4 dark matter for 48 slots.
itemdesc-alchemicalbag-red: A 32-slot bag. Wear it in a backpack slot. Upgrade it with 4 dark matter for 48 slots.
itemdesc-alchemicalbag-orange: A 32-slot bag. Wear it in a backpack slot. Upgrade it with 4 dark matter for 48 slots.
itemdesc-alchemicalbag-yellow: A 32-slot bag. Wear it in a backpack slot. Upgrade it with 4 dark matter for 48 slots.
itemdesc-alchemicalbag-green: A 32-slot bag. Wear it in a backpack slot. Upgrade it with 4 dark matter for 48 slots.
itemdesc-alchemicalbag-blue: A 32-slot bag. Wear it in a backpack slot. Upgrade it with 4 dark matter for 48 slots.
itemdesc-alchemicalbag-purple: A 32-slot bag. Wear it in a backpack slot. Upgrade it with 4 dark matter for 48 slots.
itemdesc-alchemicalbag-pink: A 32-slot bag. Wear it in a backpack slot. Upgrade it with 4 dark matter for 48 slots.
itemdesc-matterarmor-dark-head: 98% protection, 2.4 flat damage reduction, protection tier 5. Durability 10,000 that never drops: hits don't wear it, so it always protects in full.
itemdesc-matterarmor-dark-body: 98% protection, 2.4 flat damage reduction, protection tier 5. Durability 10,000 that never drops: hits don't wear it, so it always protects in full.
itemdesc-matterarmor-dark-legs: 98% protection, 2.4 flat damage reduction, protection tier 5. Durability 10,000 that never drops: hits don't wear it, so it always protects in full.
itemdesc-matterarmor-red-head: 98.5% protection, 3 flat damage reduction, protection tier 6, +3% walk speed per piece. Durability 10,000 that never drops: hits don't wear it, so it always protects in full. A full set makes you immune to fire.
itemdesc-matterarmor-red-body: 98.5% protection, 3 flat damage reduction, protection tier 6, +3% walk speed per piece. Durability 10,000 that never drops: hits don't wear it, so it always protects in full. A full set makes you immune to fire.
itemdesc-matterarmor-red-legs: 98.5% protection, 3 flat damage reduction, protection tier 6, +3% walk speed per piece. Durability 10,000 that never drops: hits don't wear it, so it always protects in full. A full set makes you immune to fire.
itemdesc-matterarmor-gem-head: 99% protection, 3.6 flat damage reduction, protection tier 7, +6% walk speed and +15% healing per piece. The helmet keeps your air full under water. A full set makes you immune to fall and fire damage. Durability 10,000 that never drops: hits don't wear it, so it always protects in full.
itemdesc-matterarmor-gem-body: 99% protection, 3.6 flat damage reduction, protection tier 7, +6% walk speed and +15% healing per piece. The chestplate makes you immune to explosions. A full set makes you immune to fall and fire damage. Durability 10,000 that never drops: hits don't wear it, so it always protects in full.
itemdesc-matterarmor-gem-legs: 99% protection, 3.6 flat damage reduction, protection tier 7, +6% walk speed and +15% healing per piece. A full set makes you immune to fall and fire damage. Durability 10,000 that never drops: hits don't wear it, so it always protects in full.
blockdesc-alchemicalfuelblock-alchemical: 9 alchemical coal: burns at 1,400 °C for 1,440 seconds.
blockdesc-alchemicalfuelblock-mobiusfuel: 9 mobius fuel: burns at 1,500 °C for 5,760 seconds.
blockdesc-alchemicalfuelblock-aeternalis: 9 aeternalis fuel: burns at 1,600 °C for 23,040 seconds.
blockdesc-alchemicalchest: 104 slots of storage (a vanilla chest has 16). Switched-on trinkets work from inside it: a Black Hole Band or Void Ring pulls loose items nearby into the chest, a Repair Talisman repairs everything in it, and a Gem of Eternal Density condenses the cheap things in it.
blockdesc-matterfurnace-dark: Smelts, fires and cooks anything with smelting data - ore straight to ingots, no crucible needed. Runs on fuel or on EMC from adjacent collectors and relays.
blockdesc-matterfurnace-red: Like the dark matter furnace, but four times as fast and hot enough for anything.
blockdesc-antimatterrelay-mk1: Stores up to 100,000 EMC from collectors, adds 1 EMC a second while it holds any, and passes up to 64 EMC a second on to condensers, furnaces and emptier relays. Sneak + right-click with an empty hand or a Klein star to take the EMC. Right-click with a Klein star to put it in: it is charged at the relay's transfer rate before anything else; right-click with an empty hand to take it out.
blockdesc-antimatterrelay-mk2: Stores up to 1,000,000 EMC from collectors, adds 3 EMC a second while it holds any, and passes up to 192 EMC a second on to condensers, furnaces and emptier relays. Sneak + right-click with an empty hand or a Klein star to take the EMC. Right-click with a Klein star to put it in: it is charged at the relay's transfer rate before anything else; right-click with an empty hand to take it out.
blockdesc-antimatterrelay-mk3: Stores up to 10,000,000 EMC from collectors, adds 10 EMC a second while it holds any, and passes up to 640 EMC a second on to condensers, furnaces and emptier relays. Sneak + right-click with an empty hand or a Klein star to take the EMC. Right-click with a Klein star to put it in: it is charged at the relay's transfer rate before anything else; right-click with an empty hand to take it out.
blockdesc-novaexplosive-catalyst: Hold right-click on it with a torch or firestarter to light it: explodes 4 seconds later with a radius of 6 blocks, and everything it breaks drops.
blockdesc-novaexplosive-cataclysm: Hold right-click on it with a torch or firestarter to light it: explodes 6 seconds later with a radius of 11 blocks, and everything it breaks drops.
blockdesc-interdictiontorch: Pushes hostile creatures out of an 8-block radius, 4 times a second, and gives off light level 20 (a torch gives 14). Needs no fuel. Arrows and other projectiles that creatures fire are turned away too.
blockdesc-pedestal-empty: Right-click with a ring, stone, amulet, talisman or watch to set it here: it then works on the area around the pedestal for free, usually 6-12 blocks (each item's description says how far).
blockdesc-pedestal-active: Working on the area around it for free. Right-click with an empty hand to take the item back.
density-filter-help: Click a slot while holding an item to list it (the item stays in your hand); with an empty hand to clear it. The gem only ever eats things worth 8 EMC or less.
density-mode-except: Eat: all cheap things except these
density-filter-only: Eats only the {0} listed kinds (if they're cheap enough).
density-filter-none: Eats every cheap thing you carry. Filter... in its tool modes lists exceptions.
density-filter-except: Eats every cheap thing except the {0} listed kinds.
heldhelp-trinket-freezeburst: Freeze burst: ice and snow within 8 blocks (32 EMC)
heldhelp-trinket-harvestburst: Harvest burst: reap and grow crops within 8 blocks (4 EMC a stage)
heldhelp-trinket-shoot-swiftwolfsrending: Call lightning where you look (832 EMC)
heldhelp-slay-hostile: Strike every hostile creature within 6 blocks (8 EMC each)
heldhelp-slay-all: Strike every creature within 6 blocks, in the air (8 EMC each)
error-nogem: Carry a Gem of Eternal Density or Void Ring to set its filter.
eye-notarget: No block chosen - sneak + right-click a block to choose one.
divining-result: {0} blocks deep: {1} EMC in total, {2} per block on average. Most valuable: {3} ({4} EMC).
furnace-burning: Burning: {0}s of heat left, {1} EMC stored
furnace-cold: Cold - add fuel or feed it EMC ({1} EMC stored)
relay-bonus: Bonus: {0} EMC/s, passes on up to {1} EMC/s
blockhelp-relay-withdraw: Take stored EMC (empty hand or Klein star)
arcana-none: All four effects are switched off (tool-mode key)
gale-outofemc: Swiftwolf's Rending Gale ran out of EMC and switched off.
gadget-charge-catalyst: Charge {0}: 3x3 tunnel {1} deep, up to {2} EMC
gadget-charge-catalytic: Charge {0}: 3x3 tunnel {1} deep, up to {2} EMC; shots radius {3}, {4} EMC each
hotkey-fire: Vintage-E: fire projectile (lenses, amulets, Ignition Ring)
cmd-emc-added: Added {0} EMC to {1}. They now have {2} EMC.
cmd-emc-removed: Took {0} EMC from {1}. They now have {2} EMC.
cmd-emc-gotadded: {0} gave you {1} EMC. You now have {2} EMC.
cmd-emc-gotremoved: {0} took {1} EMC from you. You now have {2} EMC.

diag-novalue-help: Work down the steps; most cases end at step 2. Each step links to the report or fix that does it.
diag-novalue-1: Step 1: Does the tooltip say anything at all?
diag-novalue-1-text: Hover the item. If the tooltip says 'No EMC value' (or shows a value), Vintage-E runs on your side and the only question is why that item has none: go to step 2. If there's no EMC line at all, your game hasn't got the values: rejoin (the table is sent on join and after every remap), or resend it from here.
diag-novalue-1-ok: Your game has the server's table and version, so this isn't the problem.
diag-novalue-1-bad: Your game's table or version doesn't match the server's. That alone can hide every value.
diag-novalue-2-text: Hold the item and open its report. It says which of these it is and offers the fix:
diag-novalue-2-heldvalued: You're holding {0}, which has a value ({1}). If the tooltip shows none, step 1 or step 3 is the one.
diag-novalue-2-heldnone: You're holding {0}, which has no value. Its report says why:
diag-novalue-2-blacklisted: Blacklisted: creative, technical and loot blocks, creatures, maps and story items are left without a value on purpose. If this one shouldn't be, the report offers 'Allow it'; /emc blacklist lists everything on the list.
diag-novalue-2-norecipe: Nothing makes it (a raw material, or something another mod gives you another way). The report suggests a value with a one-click 'Pin it'; otherwise /emc set <value> while holding it, or BaseValues in the settings. For a whole mod, see step 4.
diag-novalue-2-waiting: Waiting on an ingredient: it has a recipe, but an ingredient has no value yet. Each is a 'why?' link; fix the ingredient and everything made from it follows.
diag-novalue-2-loop: In a loop: it and some other items are only made from each other, so none can get a value first. Pin one of them; /emc loop lists every loop.
diag-novalue-2-gray: Gray-listed (/emc graylist): left out on purpose until a real recipe makes it. Take it off the list to let it be guessed.
diag-novalue-3: Step 3: Values are there, but not for this exact one
diag-novalue-3-text: A worn, filled or differently made version (a half-used tool, a filled bucket, a gold round shield) can differ from the plain item: /emc dump hand explains the held stack's number. Only some variants missing (one colour, one wood) has its own report:
diag-novalue-4: Step 4: A whole mod has no values
diag-novalue-4-text: The mod's report shows its coverage and the raw materials that would fix the most items at once, and can draft a compatibility file to post on the Mod DB page so it ships with Vintage-E. It also names the emcValue attribute the mod's own author could add.
diag-novalue-5: Step 5: It had a value before
diag-novalue-5-text: After a mod update or a settings change the values are mapped again (or loaded from the cache when nothing relevant changed). 'What changed' lists what the last mapping lost, changed and gained; a fresh mapping can be forced.
diag-novalue-6: Step 6: It has a value, but the table won't take it
diag-novalue-6-text: That's knowledge, not value. An item is learned by burning one (or /emc learn while holding it), and each player knows up to {0} exact versions of items that keep their contents or material. The watch shows every refusal the table made recently, and why.
diag-novalue-7-text: The bug report gathers versions, mods, the check-up, changed settings and the server log's Vintage-E lines. Post it on the Mod DB page or as a GitHub issue with the item's code and what you expected.
diag-symptoms-help: Pick the sentence that fits best; each runs just the checks for that situation.
diag-sym-tooltipnoburn: The tooltip shows a value, but the table won't burn or create it
diag-sym-tooltipnoburn-means: A value alone isn't enough. The item also mustn't be on the no-transmute list, a container with contents is protected, and creating needs you to have learned it.
diag-sym-notonlist: It isn't on the no-transmute list.
diag-sym-tooltipnoburn-also: Also: the table only takes what's on your mouse cursor; a worn tool burns for less; an item with contents burns as item + contents (or not at all when protected).
diag-sym-noclientvalues: The server has values (the log says so), but I see none in my game
diag-sym-noclientvalues-means: Then the table hasn't reached your game, or your game runs a different Vintage-E version.
diag-sym-noclientvalues-also: Also: if other players see values and you don't, it's your game, not the server. Rejoin, and look in client-main.log for Vintage-E errors.
diag-sym-aftermod: Values changed or vanished after I added or updated a mod
diag-sym-aftermod-means: Another mod's recipes and patches feed into the mapping. These show what it changed, and where it comes through.
diag-sym-afterrestart: It worked, then after a restart it didn't
diag-sym-afterrestart-means: Each start maps again (or loads the cache). Something that changed between the two starts - a mod, a value file, the settings, the game version - is the cause.
diag-sym-afterrestart-fresh: This start mapped afresh (no cache was used).
diag-sym-onlyme: It works for another player but not for me (or the other way round)
diag-sym-onlyme-means: Values are the same for everyone. What differs is knowledge, EMC, privileges, game mode, and each game's copy of the table.
diag-sym-somevariants: Some variants of an item have a value and others don't
diag-sym-somevariants-means: Variants that only look different borrow a value. Variants that change what the item is (material, metal, gem, type) don't, and need their own recipe or value.
diag-sym-somevariants-also: The report above is for the variant you hold. To fix a whole family at once, use a wildcard in BaseValues: "item:game:thing-*": <value>.
diag-sym-wrongvalue: An item has a value, but it's far too high or too low
diag-sym-wrongvalue-means: Click the item for the full story: which recipe, with which ingredient values. A value priced from a recipe that uses the item is the usual cause of a wild number.
diag-sym-containers: Containers, meals or filled things give odd values
diag-sym-containers-means: They're worth the item plus (or instead of) what's inside, depending on the contents mode, and one thing inside with no value shows as an odd total.
diag-sym-cantcreate: I can burn things but can't create the item I want
diag-sym-cantcreate-means: Creating needs the item learned, a value, enough EMC, and the item not on the no-transmute list.
diag-sym-cantcreate-also: Also: the table creates onto your cursor or into your inventory; a full inventory refuses. Exact versions (a filled bucket) are learned separately from the plain item.
diag-sym-nothing-means: Either the mapping never ran or failed, or your game never got the table.
diag-q-changes: What changed since the previous mapping
diag-changes-none: There's no earlier mapping to compare with yet (this is the world's first mapping, or the snapshot file is missing). From now on each mapping is kept for comparison.

diag-changes-why: The line under each item says where its current value comes from. A pin (/emc set), a settings change, a compatibility file switched on or off, or a mod added between the two mappings is the usual cause.
diag-next-game: These are base-game items Vintage-E doesn't value yet. That's for Vintage-E to add, so it's worth reporting:
diag-next-mod: These are {0} items made in a way Vintage-E can't read (its own machine, a custom recipe type, a drop it doesn't know). Vintage-E can be taught them with a compatibility file; the fastest way to get one is to ask:

A Transmutation Tablet with a crafting grid, made from a tablet and four red matter (it keeps the tablet's magnet).

diag-sec-startup: What other mods did at start-up
diag-q-startup: Show everything other mods did at start-up
diag-startup-step: Start-up: one of Vintage-E's own start-up steps crashed: {0}
diag-startup-step-why: The other steps still ran, so most of the mod works, but whatever that step sets up is missing. The step named 'commands' means /emc; 'network' means the client can't talk to the server; 'services' means transmutation and trinkets.
diag-startup-step-fix: This is usually a clash with another mod. Copy the bug report (Copy below) and post it on the Mod DB page; it says which step and why.
diag-startup-late: Start-up: the EMC mapping did not run at the game's normal start-up step. It ran later, when {0} happened.
diag-startup-late-why: The game runs every mod's start-up step in turn. When a mod crashes in its step, the game can stop before it reaches the mods after it, Vintage-E included. Vintage-E now notices and maps anyway, but the mod that crashed is still broken, and anything else waiting on that step may be too.
diag-startup-late-fix: Look at the start-up errors below: the mod named there is the one to update, fix (install what it needs) or remove.
diag-startup-command: Start-up: another mod had already registered /emc before Vintage-E started.
diag-startup-command-why: Two mods want the same command, so one of them loses its commands. Ctrl+H still opens this window.
diag-startup-command-fix: Find the other mod that adds /emc and remove it, or ask its author to rename the command.
diag-startup-crashes: Other mods: {0} error(s) while the game started.
diag-startup-crashes-why: These aren't Vintage-E's errors, but a mod that crashes while starting can leave items, recipes or whole start-up steps missing, and the values follow. Vintage-E's own start-up wasn't hit this time.
diag-startup-crashes-why-hit: These aren't Vintage-E's errors, but a mod that crashes while starting can stop the game from reaching the mods after it. That is the most likely reason Vintage-E had no values at the normal time. The first line of each error names the mod.
diag-startup-crashes-fix: Update or remove the mod named in the error. If the error says something is missing (a library, a dependency, a file), install it from the Mod DB: a mod that only works once another one is installed depends on it.
diag-startup-more: … and {0} more in the full start-up report.
diag-startup-skipped: Other mods: {0} were skipped by the game because something they need isn't installed: {1}
diag-startup-skipped-why: The game leaves these mods out entirely, so this doesn't break Vintage-E, but their items and recipes don't exist in this world and can't have values.
diag-startup-skipped-fix: Install what they need from the Mod DB (the name after 'needs' is a mod id), or remove them.
diag-startup-patches: Other mods: {0} JSON patch(es) failed to apply (by mod: {1}).
diag-startup-patches-why: Not Vintage-E's doing: the game reports each patch that didn't fit. The items those patches change may be missing or odd, and their values with them. The mod's author can fix the patch.
diag-startup-unresolved: Other mods: {0} recipe(s) or drop(s) name items that don't exist (by mod of the missing item: {1}).
diag-startup-unresolved-why: The game ignores those recipes, so Vintage-E can't learn from them. Usually the mod named expects another mod, or an older version of one, to be installed.
diag-startup-clean: Other mods: nothing went wrong at start-up.
diag-startup-clean-why: No mod was skipped, none crashed while starting, and every JSON patch and recipe the game loaded resolved.
doctor-noanswer: The server didn't answer the doctor within 12 seconds. Vintage-E is probably not installed or enabled on the server (in single player: in this world's mod list), or the server is still starting.
doctor-noanswer-short: No answer from the server: is Vintage-E running there?
diag-sec-health: Health: the game, the files, the players, and values that moved
diag-health-help: Checks around the mapping rather than of it. Each line says what it looked at; open one for what it means and what to do.
diag-q-health: Health checks: game version, files, join cost, players, value swings, solver, traders, variants
diag-gamever-same: Game version: {0}, the version this build of Vintage-E was tested on.
diag-gamever-unknown: Game version: couldn't compare {0} with the tested {1}.
diag-gamever-older: Game version: {0} is older than the {1} this build was tested on.
diag-gamever-older-why: An older game can lack methods the mod calls. That shows up as errors in the log, and as features that do nothing.
diag-gamever-older-fix: Update the game, or install the Vintage-E release made for your game version from the Mod DB.
diag-gamever-newer: Game version: {0} is newer than the {1} this build was tested on.
diag-gamever-newer-why: A new game version can add recipe types the mapper doesn't read yet (items made only that way get no value), and can rename the methods the look patches hook (they then do nothing, which is logged at start-up).
diag-gamever-newer-fix: Check the Mod DB for a newer Vintage-E. If there is none, post which game version you're on and what's missing.
diag-gamever-patch: Game version: {0}, a patch newer than the {1} this build was tested on.
diag-gamever-patch-why: Patch releases rarely change what the mod reads. Nothing to do unless something below is off.
diag-write-ok: Files: the mod can write to its data, cache and settings folders.
diag-write-bad: Files: {0} folder(s) the mod can't write to.
diag-write-why: The cache, the value snapshots, the bug report, drafted compatibility files and settings changed in-game all go there. When a write fails the mod logs it and carries on, so values still map, but nothing is remembered between restarts.
diag-write-fix: Check the folder's permissions and the free disk space, then run the checks again.
diag-join-ok: Join cost: the EMC table is {0} and took {1} ms to send last time.
diag-join-slow: Join cost: the EMC table is {0} and took {1} ms to send last time ({2} online).
diag-join-slow-why: Every player gets the whole table when they join and after every remap. A big table means a pause on join, and a burst of traffic when an admin remaps with many players on.
diag-join-slow-fix: Remap when few are online. If the table is huge, a mod with thousands of variants is in it; blacklisting families nobody transmutes (see the table size check) shrinks it.
diag-join-error: Join cost: the table couldn't be measured ({0}).
diag-pdata-nobody: Players: nobody is online to check.
diag-pdata-nobody-why: A player's EMC and learned items are stored with the player, so only online players can be checked. Run this while players are on.
diag-pdata-ok: Players: the data of all {0} online looks right.
diag-pdata-ok-why: Their EMC is a normal number, every learned item still exists, nobody is over the exact-knowledge limit, and no tablet filter names a missing item.
diag-pdata-found: Players: {0} thing(s) off in the data of the {1} online.
diag-pdata-dead: {0}: {1} of {2} learned items no longer exist (e.g. {3}).
diag-pdata-overcap: {0}: knows {1} exact items, over the limit of {2}.
diag-pdata-filter: {0}: a tablet filter names {1} item(s) that no longer exist.
diag-pdata-why: Learned items that no longer exist come from a removed mod: harmless, they just don't show. A player over the limit learned items before the limit was lowered; the oldest are forgotten as new ones are learned. A bad EMC number is reset to 0 the next time it changes.
diag-pdata-fix: Nothing needs doing for removed mods' items: they sit in the list harmlessly and count for nothing. A filter slot with a missing item can be cleared by clicking it in the tablet window.
diag-swing-none-yet: Value swings: no earlier mapping to compare with yet.
diag-swing-ok: Value swings: no value moved tenfold since the last mapping with the same mods.
diag-swing-found: Value swings: {0} value(s) moved tenfold or more since the last mapping, with the same mods loaded.
diag-swing-why: With the same mods and recipes, a value should come out the same each time. A tenfold swing means the solver landed somewhere else: usually a loop whose settling point depends on the order the recipes were read, or a value file or setting that changed between the two.
diag-swing-fix: If a settings file or value file changed, this is expected. Otherwise pin the item (the first one listed is the loudest), remap, and include the list in a bug report: a swing with nothing changed is a solver bug.
diag-solver-ok: Solver: every recipe whose ingredients all have values gave its output one.
diag-solver-found: Solver: {0} item(s) have a recipe whose ingredients all have values, yet got no value.
diag-solver-why: The mapper saw the recipe and every ingredient is valued, so only the solver itself stopped the output: the item sits in a value loop it couldn't settle, or its value came out below the smallest the solver keeps (a recipe that gives back far more than it takes, like a block uncrafted into shingles, drives it there).
diag-solver-floor: came out below the floor, or the recipe was skipped
diag-solver-fix: Pin the item at what its ingredients add up to (the trace shows them), and include the list in a bug report: this is exactly the kind of case the solver should handle.
diag-solver-cache: Solver: the values came from the cache, which keeps no recipes. Run /emc recalc, then check again.
diag-traderrecipe-ok: Trader prices: no item is priced from a trader above what a recipe for it costs.
diag-traderrecipe-found: Trader prices: {0} item(s) are priced from a trader above what a recipe with valued ingredients costs.
diag-traderrecipe-why: The cheapest real way to get an item is its value, and buying from a trader counts. So a trader price below the recipe's cost is right. These are the other way round: the trader's price won although a recipe makes the item for less, so crafting one and burning it gives EMC for nothing. The mapper read the recipe too late or threw it away (a loop, a processing recipe missing an ingredient, a recipe the collector doesn't fully understand).
diag-traderrecipe-fix: If the recipe's cost looks right, pin the item at it. Include the list in a bug report so the mapper can be taught the recipe.
diag-vspread-ok: Variants: every value copied from a look-alike variant comes from a family that agrees on it.
diag-vspread-found: Variants: {0} value(s) were copied from a look-alike variant in a family that doesn't agree ({1}).
diag-vspread-why: When nothing makes an item, the mapper copies the value of a variant that differs only in look (a copyAcross group). That's safe when the family agrees. Here the family's own-valued members disagree by more than half, so the copy took whichever member came first, and the item may be worth a lot more or less than it says. An attribute behind many of these (growth stage, age, state) isn't look-only at all and belongs in neverAcross.
diag-vspread-fix: Check the item's trace and pin it if the copy is wrong. For an attribute with many entries, add it to neverAcross in the value file (variantGuessing) so the guesser uses the family's middle value instead.
diag-hotkeys-ok: Hotkeys: no other hotkey shares a key with Vintage-E's.
diag-hotkeys-found: Hotkeys: {0} of Vintage-E's hotkeys share a key with another hotkey.
diag-hotkeys-why: When two hotkeys of the same kind share a key, the game runs one and the other does nothing, or both run. That's why a key 'does nothing' or opens the wrong thing.
diag-hotkeys-fix: Rebind one of them in Settings → Controls (Vintage-E's are listed under its name: fire projectile, set value, EMC doctor).
diag-harmony-ok: Other mods' patches: no other mod patches the game methods Vintage-E relies on.
diag-harmony-ok-why: The shape loaders the looks hook, item tooltips, inventories and damage are untouched by other mods' Harmony patches.
diag-harmony-found: Other mods' patches: {0} game method(s) Vintage-E relies on are patched by other mods.
